correctness.rationale: Definitions and quantifiers have been checked for all cycle sizes n>=4 including empty and full domains. The published cycle-partial-isometry dihedral restriction lemma is valid above rank two and independently inspected. The proof shows self-inverse restrictions on >=3 vertices must come from unique global group involutions: a nonidentity dihedral element cannot fix >=3 vertices. Their invariant subsets have known (1+z)^f(1+z^2)^t cycle polynomials. The low-rank coefficients 1,n,2*C(n,2) are recomputed directly; odd corrections n(1+z), even corrections n+1+n*z+n*z^2 follow exactly. Direct metric enumeration for n=4..9, complete comparison of metric partial injections with dihedral restrictions for n=4..7, and independently deduplicated dihedral enumeration for n=4..12 match the universal theorem and each relevant coefficient. These bounded checks corroborate rather than prove the universal formula.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The nilpotent locus and self-inverse locus intersect only in the empty partial map: a nonempty self-inverse satisfies α²=id_D and therefore cannot be nilpotent. The fence object lacks the metric and dihedral extension structure, so has no implication or reduction. Fernandes–Paulista provides a powerful premise used by the proof but not the claimed formula: deriving this requires analyzing the global involution cycle structure and an explicit parity-sensitive correction at ranks zero, one, and two. Prior overall counts cannot be inverted to obtain this rank distribution.

originality.rationale: A complete direct comparison with the three closely related available primary preprints identifies their structural, cardinality, Green-relation, and presentation statements but no self-inverse whole-monoid domain-rank formula. The 2022 cycle-partial-isometry Lemma 1.1 supplies the ambient extension and uniqueness premises; standard involution cycle polynomials plus a new exact low-rank duplicate correction are additionally required to determine the asserted polynomial. An accessible earlier nilpotency-index census of the same monoid cannot cover self-inverse ranks, because a nonempty self-inverse partial map has all even powers nonempty. A separate result on self-inverse fence partial automorphisms concerns a nonreducible different object. Targeted public literature, indexed finding, and exact-sequence searches found no competing result. Residual risks are recorded and no absolute uniqueness assertion is made.
residual_risks: The full text of the 2022 M.Sc. thesis Partial Isometries of Some Simple Connected Graphs was not obtained. It is plausible prior text about precisely these objects, although its publicly available descriptions do not mention self-inverse enumeration.
Unindexed specialist articles, independent unpublished derivations, or a sequence database table may contain part or all of the result; targeted search was not a uniqueness certificate.
The ambient dihedral restriction theorem and standard involution cycle index are known; originality concerns only the explicit all-rank self-inverse specialization and low-rank correction.

value.rationale: Self-inverseness is canonical in any inverse monoid, and its rank-refined population is not recoverable from monoid cardinality, ordinary Green theory, or rank of generating sets. The formula is a complete exact natural invariant for all finite cycles, showing the even/odd orbit-type transition, nontrivial low-rank overcount corrections, and the asymptotic dominance of the 2^n partial identities among self-inverse elements. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere table recomputation; it addresses the full-domain-size spectrum and its structural source.
